newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill eight rebels in Algiers.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill eight rebels in Algiers.

text.p: Algerian security forces shot dead at least eight Moslem guerrillas, members of the radical Armed Islamic Group (GIA), in a fierce gunbattle in the Casbah, the ancient heart of Algiers, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
Acting on a tipoff, crack forces on Wednesday stormed a guerrilla hide-out near a mosque in the Casbah killing GIA local leader Amara Yacine and five of his follwers, said El Watan newspaper.
Security forces snipers shot dead two other GIA members who took refuge in a separate hideout in the Casbah, El Watan said.
Liberte newspaper put the number of dead guerrillas, who were armed with assault rifles, automatic pistols and grenades, at nine.
The operation, for which security forces ringed the Casbah and evacuated some families for safety, lasted about seven hours, Algerian newspapers said.

El Watan said the slain GIA local leader escaped death a few months ago in an encounter with security forces in the Casbah. His brother Hamid then rushed to rescue him by unleashing a hail of gunfire to cover his retreat into the maze of narrow streets.
Hamid and dozens of other militants have been killed since then, the newspaper said.
President Liamine Zeroual said late last month the security situation was improving and the state had all the means to wipe out Moslem rebels who still reject his offer of clemency.

Algerian government forces and Moslem guerrillas have been locked in conflict since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. An estimated 50,000 people have died in the violence.
